name: Trie (Prefix Tree)
description: A tree structure where each path from root to a node represents a string prefix, enabling fast prefix-based lookups, autocomplete, and word search that a hashmap of full strings can't do efficiently.
core_technique: Each node holds a map/array of children keyed by character, plus a flag marking whether a complete word ends at that node. Inserting a word walks/creates nodes character by character. Searching for a word or a prefix walks the same path and checks either the end-of-word flag (exact match) or just that the path exists (prefix match).
common_pitfalls: Confusing 'does this prefix exist' with 'does this exact word exist' - these need different checks (path exists vs. path exists AND end-of-word flag is true); not handling the search for wildcard characters (e.g. 'Add and Search Word' with '.') which requires branching DFS instead of a simple linear walk; using a hashmap of children when a fixed-size array (e.g. 26 for lowercase letters) would be simpler and faster for constrained alphabets.

example_problems.title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
example_problems.why_it_fits: Direct implementation - insert, search (exact word), and startsWith (prefix) as the three core trie operations.

example_problems.title: Word Search II
example_problems.why_it_fits: Build a trie of the target words, then DFS through the grid while simultaneously walking the trie - pruning grid paths early the moment they stop matching any trie prefix, avoiding a separate search per word.

example_problems.title: Add and Search Word
example_problems.why_it_fits: Standard trie search, but a '.' wildcard means trying all children at that position - requires DFS/backtracking layered on top of the trie walk instead of a single deterministic path.

additional_considerations: For grid-search problems combining a trie with DFS (like Word Search II), removing words from the trie (or marking them found) once matched avoids re-reporting duplicates and can prune the search further. Always clarify the alphabet size upfront - it determines whether an array-based or hashmap-based children structure is more appropriate.
